sentences.en: Absolutely.

sentences.en: I mean, it has these connotations of, you know, Soviet-era construction,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它带有这种暗示，你知道的，苏联时期的建设，

sentences.zh: 有时是第三世界建设，所有这些负面联想。

sentences.en: This is Professor Adrian Forty, author of the excellent book, Concrete and Culture.
sentences.zh: 这是阿德里安·福蒂教授，优秀著作《混凝土与文化》的作者。

sentences.en: It has a bad name.
sentences.zh: 它名声不好。

sentences.en: Apart from aesthetic criticisms, concrete buildings present environmental concerns.
sentences.zh: 除了美学上的批评，混凝土建筑还带来了环境问题。

sentences.en: A lot of these buildings were built at a time when energy was cheap,
sentences.zh: 其中许多建筑建于能源便宜的时期，

sentences.en: and they use up an awful lot of energy to heat and cool them.
sentences.zh: 它们消耗了大量的能源来供暖和制冷。

sentences.en: Concrete buildings were built with the illusion of plenty,
sentences.zh: 混凝土建筑是在富足的幻觉下建造的，

sentences.en: that we will always have enough energy to build and heat and cool these massive, inefficient structures.
sentences.zh: 认为我们将永远有足够的能源来建造、供暖和制冷这些庞大、低效的结构。

sentences.en: As harsh as it looks, concrete is an utterly optimistic building material.
sentences.zh: 尽管它看起来很严酷，但混凝土是一种绝对乐观的建筑材料。

sentences.en: Arguably too optimistic.
sentences.zh: 可以说过于乐观了。

sentences.en: Really, from the 1920s, it was seen as being the material that would change the world.
sentences.zh: 实际上，从20世纪20年代起，它就被视为将改变世界的材料。

sentences.en: It had the potential to build things in a way that hadn't been seen before.
sentences.zh: 它具有以从未见过的方式建造东西的潜力。

sentences.en: Concrete was this material that seemed boundless, readily available in vast quantities,
sentences.zh: 混凝土这种材料似乎没有界限，随时可以大量供应，

sentences.en: and it could create massive spaces unlike any other material.
sentences.zh: 并且可以创造出与其他任何材料都不同的巨大空间。

sentences.en: So concrete sprang up everywhere.
sentences.zh: 因此混凝土如雨后春笋般随处涌现。

sentences.en: It's the second most heavily consumed product in the world.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上消费量第二大的产品。

sentences.en: The only thing we consume more of than concrete is water.
sentences.zh: 我们消耗量比混凝土多的唯一东西是水。

sentences.en: We use concrete for sidewalks, bridges, tunnels, and highways.
sentences.zh: 我们将混凝土用于人行道、桥梁、隧道和高速公路。

sentences.en: And of course, for giant buildings.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有巨大的建筑。

sentences.en: Whether we're talking about stadia or auditoria.
sentences.zh: 无论我们是在谈论体育场还是礼堂。

sentences.en: Or condominia, or gymnasia, or planetaria.
sentences.zh: 或者公寓、体育馆或天文馆。

sentences.en: So historically, government programs all over the world loved concrete.
sentences.zh: 因此，从历史上看，世界各地的政府项目都喜欢混凝土。

sentences.en: Particularly in Soviet Russia, but also later in Europe, North America.
sentences.zh: 特别是在苏联俄罗斯，但后来也在欧洲和北美。

sentences.en: It was used for welfare, welfare state projects.
sentences.zh: 它被用于福利，福利国家项目。

sentences.en: Concrete presented the most efficient way to house huge numbers of people.
sentences.zh: 混凝土为容纳大量人口提供了最有效的方式。

sentences.en: And philosophically, it was seen as humble, capable, and honeSt.
sentences.zh: 从哲学上讲，它被视为谦逊、能干和诚实。

sentences.en: Concrete was just out there in all of its rough glory, not hiding behind any paint or layers.
sentences.zh: 混凝土以其粗犷的荣耀展现出来，不隐藏在任何油漆或层后面。

sentences.en: Saying, here I am, love me or hate me.
sentences.zh: 仿佛在说，我在这里，爱我还是恨我。

sentences.en: And as concrete buildings came to signify humility, honesty, and integrity,
sentences.zh: 随着混凝土建筑开始象征着谦逊、诚实和正直，

sentences.en: they were erected all over the world as housing projects, courthouses, schools, churches, hospitals, and city halls.
sentences.zh: 它们作为住房项目、法院、学校、教堂、医院和市政厅在世界各地拔地而起。

sentences.en: You'll stand outside, and a tour bus will go by, and there'll be,
sentences.zh: 你站在外面，一辆观光巴士开过，就会听到，

sentences.en: ladies and gentlemen, voted the most ugliest building in the world, Boston City Hall.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，被投票选为世界上最丑陋的建筑，波士顿市政厅。

sentences.en: How do you compete with that?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能与之竞争呢？

sentences.en: Chris Grimley is up against a lot, but he's trying to restore Boston City Hall's reputation.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·格里姆利面临着很多困难，但他正试图恢复波士顿市政厅的名誉。

sentences.en: My name is Chris Grimley.
sentences.zh: 我叫克里斯·格里姆利。

sentences.en: I'm with my fellow heroic people, Mark Pasnick and Michael Kubo.
sentences.zh: 我和我的英雄同伴马克·帕斯尼克和迈克尔·库博在一起。

sentences.en: Chris, Mark, and Michael have embarked on what they call the heroic project,
sentences.zh: 克里斯、马克和迈克尔开始了他们所谓的英雄项目，

sentences.en: chronicling the concrete structures in and around Boston.
sentences.zh: 记录波士顿及其周边的混凝土结构。

sentences.en: Rather than referring to these concrete buildings as brutalist,
sentences.zh: 他们更愿意使用“英雄”一词，而不是将这些混凝土建筑称为野兽派，

sentences.en: they prefer the term heroic.
sentences.zh: 因为就像许多超级英雄一样，

sentences.en: Because like so many superheroes,
sentences.zh: 这些结构有着最好、最高尚的意图，

sentences.en: these structures have the best, most noble intentions,
sentences.zh: 但却被严重误解了。

sentences.en: but are sorely misunderstood.
sentences.zh: 此外，总的来说，野兽派是一个宏大而宽泛的标签，

sentences.en: Also, just generally, brutalism is a big, broad label
sentences.zh: 在建筑学中经常被不一致地使用。

sentences.en: that gets used inconsistently in architecture.
sentences.zh: 人们往往对一个精确的定义意见不一。

sentences.en: People tend to disagree on one precise definition.
sentences.zh: 野兽派这个名字听起来也很强烈，

sentences.en: The name brutalism also just sounds intense,
sentences.zh: 尽管它实际上与残暴无关。

sentences.en: even though it's not actually related to brutality.
sentences.zh: 它来自béton brut，这是一个法文词，意为清水混凝土。

sentences.en: It comes from béton brut, which is a French term for raw concrete.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，对这些人来说，英雄感觉是一个更好的词，

sentences.en: In any case, to these guys, heroic feels like a better term,
sentences.zh: 特别是在波士顿，混凝土建筑曾从天而降并拯救了世界。

sentences.en: especially in Boston, where concrete architecture swooped in and saved the day.
sentences.zh: 你必须把波士顿放在50年代末、1960年代的背景下去看。

sentences.en: You have to situate Boston in late 50s, 1960s.
sentences.zh: 它是美国的第一个城市。

sentences.en: It is America's first city.
sentences.zh: 好吧……

sentences.en: Well...
sentences.zh: 它是美国最具历史意义的城市。

sentences.en: It is America's most historic city.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，并不是真的，但我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: Again, not really, but I get your point.
sentences.zh: 然而它却发现自己处于低谷之中。

sentences.en: And yet it finds itself in the doldruMs.
sentences.zh: 波士顿和许多其他美国城市一样，

sentences.en: Boston, like a lot of other American cities,
sentences.zh: 受到制造业工作岗位流失和白人群飞至郊区的困扰。

sentences.en: was plagued by a loss of manufacturing jobs and white flight to the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，波士顿拥有全国最高的房产税，

sentences.en: And for decades, Boston had the highest property taxes in the nation,
sentences.zh: 几乎没有任何发展。

sentences.en: and almost no development.
sentences.zh: 公民当局认识到必须采取行动，

sentences.en: There is this recognition from civic authorities that something needs to be done,
sentences.zh: 而且必须迅速采取行动。

sentences.en: and something needs to be done quickly.
sentences.zh: 因此，波士顿制定了一个议程，让这座城市再次伟大，

sentences.en: So Boston sets an agenda to make the city great again,
sentences.zh: 使用宏大、高耸、能干、完全现代的建筑，当然，它们是由混凝土制成的。

sentences.en: with big, soaring, capable, thoroughly modern buildings made, of course, out of concrete.
sentences.zh: 尽管其中一些建筑受到了赞誉，但其他的则确实没有。

sentences.en: And though some of these buildings were celebrated, others were really not.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为波士顿混凝土现代主义第三轨道的是市政厅。

sentences.en: What we call the third rail of Boston concrete modernism is City Hall.
sentences.zh: 当波士顿市政厅于1968年建成时，评论家们对这种混凝土风格感到反感。

sentences.en: When Boston City Hall was built in 1968, critics were put off by this concrete style.
sentences.zh: 它被称为疏离和寒冷。

sentences.en: It was called alienating and cold.
sentences.zh: 由于它是一座政府建筑，

sentences.en: And since it was a government building,
sentences.zh: 这种批评变得无法从政治中剥离出来。

sentences.en: this criticism became impossible to remove from politics.
sentences.zh: 波士顿市政厅成为了一个政治筹码。

sentences.en: Boston City Hall became a political pawn.
sentences.zh: 市长和市议会成员不断试图赢得公众的支持，

sentences.en: Mayors and city council members kept trying to win public support
sentences.zh: 承诺摆脱这座建筑，

sentences.en: with promises to get rid of the building,
sentences.zh: 就像约翰·托宾竞选市议员时所做的那样。

sentences.en: like John Tobin did when he ran for city council.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是约翰·托宾。

sentences.en: Hi everybody, this is John Tobin.
sentences.zh: 感谢访问votejohntobin.com。

sentences.en: Thanks for visiting votejohntobin.com.
sentences.zh: 感谢访问 votejohntobin.com。

sentences.en: Here we are on City Hall Plaza in front of Boston City Hall.
sentences.zh: 现在我们位于波士顿市政厅广场，就在波士顿市政厅的前面。

sentences.en: I'm not an architect, but I know bad architecture when I see it.
sentences.zh: 我不是建筑师，但坏建筑我一眼就能认出来。

sentences.en: This is a bad building, and I think we can do a lot by knocking this building down.
sentences.zh: 这是一座糟糕的建筑，我觉得我们可以通过把它推倒来做很多事情。

sentences.en: Former Mayor Thomas Menino actually started a study to really look into tearing it down.
sentences.zh: 前市长托马斯·梅尼诺实际上曾发起一项研究，认真探讨过拆除它的可行性。

sentences.en: It turned out as a result of the study that you would need something like a nuclear-grade weapon,
sentences.zh: 研究结果表明，你可能需要某种核武器级别的武器，

sentences.en: basically, to destroy this building,
sentences.zh: 基本上才能摧毁这座建筑，

sentences.en: because it was so heavily overbuilt in concrete.
sentences.zh: 因为它的混凝土结构实在是太厚重了。

sentences.en: And so, when they couldn't tear down City Hall, officials chose to ignore it.
sentences.zh: 因此，既然无法拆除市政厅，官员们便选择视而不见。

sentences.en: People that occupied the building for decades and decades didn't like it,
sentences.zh: 几十年来一直占据这座建筑的人们并不喜欢它，

sentences.en: and so they didn't invest money into the building,
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有在这栋建筑上投入资金，

sentences.en: and effectively wanted to see the building go away.
sentences.zh: 实际上是希望这座建筑能自行消失。

sentences.en: This is called active neglect, and it happens with a lot of concrete buildings.
sentences.zh: 这被称为积极忽视，许多混凝土建筑都会遭遇这种情况。

sentences.en: They are intentionally unrepaired, unrenovated, and uncared for.
sentences.zh: 它们故意得不到修复、翻新和照料。

sentences.en: Which only makes the building more ugly, and then more hated, and then more ignored,
sentences.zh: 这只会让建筑变得更加丑陋，进而更加招人厌恶，更加被忽视，

sentences.en: and creates this vicious cycle where the public hate of Boston City Hall feeds itself.
sentences.zh: 并形成这样一个恶性循环：公众对波士顿市政厅的厌恶情绪不断滋长。

sentences.en: And then the discussion years on really became about what the original architects had done wrong,
sentences.zh: 随后的几年里，讨论的焦点真正变成了最初的建筑师究竟哪里做错了，

sentences.en: as if this were not a failure of maintenance, but a failure of the initial design.
sentences.zh: 就好像这不是维护不善的问题，而是初始设计出了问题。

sentences.en: When people built these mammoth concrete structures, no one really thought about maintenance.
sentences.zh: 当人们建造这些庞大的混凝土结构时，没有人真正考虑过维护问题。

sentences.en: They seemed indestructible.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来坚不可摧。

sentences.en: In the early days of concrete, people assumed that this was an everlasting material,
sentences.zh: 在混凝土使用的早期，人们认为这是一种永恒的材料，

sentences.en: that wouldn't need any attention at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不需要任何维护。

sentences.en: And, I mean, that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这种想法是错误的。

sentences.en: We know that it does need to be looked after.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它的确需要有人照看。

sentences.en: It does deteriorate.
sentences.zh: 它确实会退化。

sentences.en: It does decay.
sentences.zh: 它确实会腐蚀。

sentences.en: But it can be hard to tell when concrete is decaying.
sentences.zh: 但混凝土何时开始腐蚀，有时很难分辨。

sentences.en: If you think of brick and timber, the decay takes place on the surface of them.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想砖石和木材，它们的腐蚀发生在表面。

sentences.en: But with concrete, the deterioration is internal.
sentences.zh: 但对于混凝土来说，劣化是内在的。

sentences.en: Concrete deteriorates chemically from the inside out.
sentences.zh: 混凝土从内到外发生着化学上的劣化。

sentences.en: Part of this has to do with the metal reinforcements that help hold up most concrete buildings.
sentences.zh: 部分原因与支撑大多数混凝土建筑的金属加固材料有关。

sentences.en: The rebar, well, it can ruSt.
sentences.zh: 钢筋，嗯，它会生锈。

sentences.en: And the rust eats away at the overall structure.
sentences.zh: 而铁锈会蚕食整个结构。

sentences.en: But, Adrian Forty says, tearing them down is not the answer.
sentences.zh: 不过，阿德里安·福蒂表示，把它们拆掉并不是解决办法。

sentences.en: Because as soon as you tear them down, then you have a problem, first of all,
sentences.zh: 因为一旦你把它们拆掉，你首先就会遇到一个问题，

sentences.en: with what you do with the detritus that's left.
sentences.zh: 那就是如何处理剩下的残渣碎屑。

sentences.en: And secondly, you've got to replace them with something else and use up a whole lot more energy
sentences.zh: 其次，你必须用别的东西来替代它们，这会消耗更多的能源，

sentences.en: and create a lot more CO2 in building something in their place.
sentences.zh: 并在原址建造替代物时产生更多的二氧化碳。

sentences.en: They already used up all that energy when they were made.
sentences.zh: 它们在建造时已经消耗了所有的能量。

sentences.en: They're already there.
sentences.zh: 它们已经立在那里了。

sentences.en: We can adapt these buildings to make them greener
sentences.zh: 我们可以改造这些建筑，让它们变得更环保，

sentences.en: and make them more appealing places to be by adding windows, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如通过增加窗户，让它们成为更具吸引力的场所。

sentences.en: But basically, Professor Forty thinks we can all develop the capacity
sentences.zh: 但基本上，福蒂教授认为我们都可以培养出一种能力，

sentences.en: to love these concrete brutes in all their hulking glory.
sentences.zh: 去热爱这些笨重的混凝土庞然大物及其雄伟的姿态。

sentences.en: Yeah, sure, people can learn to love anything.
sentences.zh: 没错，当然，人们可以学会去爱任何东西。

sentences.en: But, you know, as with any art form,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，就像任何艺术形式一样，

sentences.en: whether it's opera or painting or literature,
sentences.zh: 无论是歌剧、绘画还是文学，

sentences.en: the more you know about it, the more you'll get out of it,
sentences.zh: 你对它了解得越多，从中收获的就越多，

sentences.en: the more you'll appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 你就会越发欣赏它。

sentences.en: And this is especially true of concrete buildings.
sentences.zh: 混凝土建筑尤其如此。

sentences.en: Architecture students appreciate them because they know
sentences.zh: 建筑专业的学生之所以欣赏它们，是因为他们知道

sentences.en: that concrete actually requires a hell of a lot of skill and finesse to work with.
sentences.zh: 使用混凝土其实需要极高的技巧和精湛的工艺。

sentences.en: To do architecture in concrete is proof that you really are an architect.
sentences.zh: 用混凝土进行建筑设计，证明了你确实是一名真正的建筑师。

sentences.en: It's the test of being an architect.
sentences.zh: 这是对是否具备建筑师资格的考验。

sentences.en: With a concrete building, every little detail needs to be calculated in advance.
sentences.zh: 对于混凝土建筑，每一个微小的细节都需要提前计算好。

sentences.en: Concrete is wildly intimidating to work with.
sentences.zh: 使用混凝土进行创作会让人感到无比敬畏。

sentences.en: Once you pour it, there's no going back.
sentences.zh: 一旦浇筑下去，就再也没有回头路了。

sentences.en: With a concrete building, it's like the result of an immaculate conception.
sentences.zh: 对于混凝土建筑来说，它就像是无瑕受孕的产物。

sentences.en: The whole thing is an integral, monolithic whole, and it has to be right.
sentences.zh: 整个建筑是一个不可分割的整体，而且必须做到完美无缺。

sentences.en: And aside from the interesting design challenges it poses,
sentences.zh: 除了它带来的有趣设计挑战之外，

sentences.en: concrete itself as a material can be subtly beautiful if you look closely.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细观察，混凝土作为一种材料本身就可以展现出一种微妙的美。

sentences.en: You know, what we think of as just a monolithic, consistent, homogenous texture
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们认为只是单一、一致且同质的质感，

sentences.en: is actually really rich and has a lot of interest
sentences.zh: 当你走近去细细端详时，

sentences.en: when you actually go up to it and consider it.
sentences.zh: 其实真的非常丰富且充满趣味。

sentences.en: Sarah Briggs-Ramsey, the one I spoke with at Berkeley's Worcester Hall,
sentences.zh: 莎拉·布里格斯-拉姆齐，就是我在伯克利的伍斯特大厅采访的那位，

sentences.en: did a year-long project traveling around the world,
sentences.zh: 曾进行过一项为期一年的环球项目，

sentences.en: It's like the background of all the cities, but no one actually stands to look.

sentences.en: We call the city a concrete jungle to talk about the artificialness of the urban landscape.

sentences.en: But concrete can actually be a very natural expression of the environment.
sentences.zh: 但混凝土实际上可以成为对环境非常自然的表达。

sentences.en: Concrete's color and texture can be dictated by local climate, local earth, and local rock.
sentences.zh: 混凝土的颜色和质感可以由当地的气候、当地的土壤和当地的岩石来决定。

sentences.en: and that's the ground from the site.
sentences.zh: 那就是来自该基地的土壤颜色。

sentences.en: Concrete can also be an expression of local style and custom,
sentences.zh: 混凝土也可以成为地方风格和风俗的表达，

sentences.en: like how UK concrete has big, thick, textured chunks of rock,
sentences.zh: 比如英国的混凝土有大块、厚实、具质感的岩石颗粒，

sentences.en: while Japanese concrete is very fine and flat.
sentences.zh: 而日本的混凝土则非常细腻平整。

sentences.en: But the beauty of concrete architecture is all the better

sentences.en: when you can just observe the buildings like pieces of sculpture,

sentences.zh: 这就引入了混凝土令人意想不到的盟友——摄影。
